passages.text: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, To those who through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ have received a faith as precious as ours: Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter writes this letter.
Simon Peter is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Simon Peter is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
He writes to people who have received faith.
Their faith is as precious as the faith of the apostles.
They received this faith through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ.
Simon Peter prays for them.
He asks that grace be multiplied to them.
He asks that peace be multiplied to them.
He says grace and peace come through knowing God.
He says grace and peace come through knowing Jesus, our Lord.
passages.original: Συμεὼν Πέτρος δοῦλος καὶ ἀπόστολος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ Τοῖς ἰσότιμον ἡμῖν λαχοῦσιν πίστιν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ Σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη πληθυνθείη ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν

passages.text: His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence.
passages.sermon:
God has divine power.
God has given us everything we need for life.
God has given us everything we need for godliness.
God gives these things through knowing Him.
God called us.
God called us by His own glory.
God called us by His own excellence.
passages.original: Ὡς τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν τῆς θείας δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ τὰ πρὸς ζωὴν καὶ εὐσέβειαν δεδωρημένης διὰ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ καλέσαντος ἡμᾶς ἰδίᾳ δόξῃ καὶ ἀρετῇ

passages.text: Through these He has given us His precious and magnificent promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, now that you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.
passages.sermon:
God has given us precious and great promises through Jesus Christ.
God gives these promises so we may share in His divine nature.
We now share in God's nature because we have escaped the world's corruption.
This corruption comes from evil desires in the world.
passages.original: δι’ ὧν τὰ τίμια καὶ μέγιστα ἡμῖν ἐπαγγέλματα δεδώρηται ἵνα διὰ τούτων γένησθε θείας κοινωνοὶ φύσεως ἀποφυγόντες τῆς ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ φθορᾶς

passages.text: For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge; and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, perseverance; and to perseverance, godliness; and to godliness, brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness, love.
passages.sermon:
God has given us everything we need for life and godliness.
He has done this through His divine power.
He has called us by His own glory and excellence.
Because of this, make every effort.
Add virtue to your faith.
Add knowledge to your virtue.
Add self-control to your knowledge.
Add perseverance to your self-control.
Add godliness to your perseverance.
Add brotherly kindness to your godliness.
Add love to your brotherly kindness.
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο δὲ σπουδὴν πᾶσαν παρεισενέγκαντες ἐπιχορηγήσατε ἐν τῇ πίστει ὑμῶν τὴν ἀρετήν ἐν δὲ τῇ ἀρετῇ τὴν γνῶσιν ἐν δὲ τῇ γνώσει τὴν ἐγκράτειαν ἐν δὲ τῇ ἐγκρατείᾳ τὴν ὑπομονήν ἐν δὲ τῇ ὑπομονῇ τὴν εὐσέβειαν ἐν δὲ τῇ εὐσεβείᾳ τὴν φιλαδελφίαν ἐν δὲ τῇ φιλαδελφίᾳ τὴν ἀγάπην

passages.text: For if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
These qualities are faith, virtue, knowledge, self-control, perseverance, godliness, brotherly kindness, and love.
If you have these qualities, you will not be idle.
If you have these qualities, you will not be unfruitful.
If you grow in these qualities, you will be effective.
If you grow in these qualities, you will be productive.
These qualities help you in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ταῦτα γὰρ ὑμῖν ὑπάρχοντα καὶ πλεονάζοντα οὐκ ἀργοὺς οὐδὲ ἀκάρπους καθίστησιν εἰς τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπίγνωσιν

passages.text: But whoever lacks these traits is nearsighted to the point of blindness, having forgotten that he has been cleansed from his past sins.
passages.sermon:
A person who does not have these qualities is spiritually blind.
This person cannot see clearly.
This person has forgotten something important.
This person has forgotten that God cleansed him from his past sins.
passages.original: ᾧ γὰρ μὴ πάρεστιν ταῦτα τυφλός ἐστιν μυωπάζων λήθην λαβὼν τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ τῶν πάλαι αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτιῶν

passages.text: Therefore, brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure. For if you practice these things you will never stumble, and you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, God has called you and chosen you.
You must work hard to make your calling and election sure.
If you do these things, you will never stumble.
God will give you a rich welcome.
You will enter the eternal kingdom.
This kingdom belongs to our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Διὸ μᾶλλον ἀδελφοί σπουδάσατε βεβαίαν ὑμῶν τὴν κλῆσιν καὶ ἐκλογὴν ποιεῖσθαι ταῦτα γὰρ ποιοῦντες οὐ μὴ πταίσητέ ποτε οὕτως γὰρ πλουσίως ἐπιχορηγηθήσεται ὑμῖν ἡ εἴσοδος εἰς τὴν αἰώνιον βασιλείαν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν καὶ Σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Therefore I will always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.
passages.sermon:
I am Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ.
I will always remind you of these things.
You already know these things.
You are established in the truth you now have.
passages.original: Διὸ μελλήσω ἀεὶ ὑμᾶς ὑπομιμνῄσκειν περὶ τούτων καίπερ εἰδότας καὶ ἐστηριγμένους ἐν τῇ παρούσῃ ἀληθείᾳ

passages.text: I think it is right to refresh your memory as long as I live in the tent of my body, because I know that this tent will soon be laid aside, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.
passages.sermon:
Peter is the speaker.
Peter is a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter writes to believers.
Peter believes it is right to remind the believers of important truths.
Peter will do this as long as he lives in his body.
Peter calls his body a tent.
Peter knows he will soon leave his body.
Peter knows this because the Lord Jesus Christ has shown him.
passages.original: δίκαιον δὲ ἡγοῦμαι ἐφ’ ὅσον εἰμὶ ἐν τούτῳ τῷ σκηνώματι διεγείρειν ὑμᾶς ἐν ὑπομνήσει εἰδὼς ὅτι ταχινή ἐστιν ἡ ἀπόθεσις τοῦ σκηνώματός μου καθὼς καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐδήλωσέν μοι

passages.text: And I will make every effort to ensure that after my departure, you will be able to recall these things at all times.
passages.sermon:
Peter is the speaker.
Peter is a leader among the apostles of Jesus Christ.
Peter will soon die and leave the believers.
Peter will work hard for the believers.
Peter will do everything he can.
Peter wants the believers to remember these teachings.
Peter wants the believers to remember these teachings after he dies.
Peter wants the believers to remember these teachings at all times.
passages.original: σπουδάσω δὲ καὶ ἑκάστοτε ἔχειν ὑμᾶς μετὰ τὴν ἐμὴν ἔξοδον τὴν τούτων μνήμην ποιεῖσθαι

passages.text: For we did not follow cleverly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.
passages.sermon:
We did not follow clever stories.
We did not use invented tales.
We made known to you the power of our Lord Jesus Christ.
We told you about the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
We saw His majesty with our own eyes.
We were eyewitnesses of His greatness.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ σεσοφισμένοις μύθοις ἐξακολουθήσαντες ἐγνωρίσαμεν ὑμῖν τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν ἀλλ’ ἐπόπται γενηθέντες τῆς ἐκείνου μεγαλειότητος

passages.text: For He received honor and glory from God the Father when the voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
God the Father gave Jesus honor and glory.
A voice came to Jesus from the Majestic Glory.
The voice said, “This is My beloved Son.
I am well pleased with Him.”
passages.original: λαβὼν γὰρ παρὰ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν φωνῆς ἐνεχθείσης αὐτῷ τοιᾶσδε ὑπὸ τῆς μεγαλοπρεποῦς δόξης Ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός μου οὗτός ἐστιν εἰς ὃν ἐγὼ εὐδόκησα

passages.text: And we ourselves heard this voice from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.
passages.sermon: We were with Jesus on the holy mountain.\r\nWe heard a voice from heaven.\r\nWe heard this voice ourselves.
passages.original: καὶ ταύτην τὴν φωνὴν ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐνεχθεῖσαν σὺν αὐτῷ ὄντες ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ ὄρει

passages.text: We also have the word of the prophets as confirmed beyond doubt. And you will do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
passages.sermon:
We have the word of the prophets.
God has confirmed this word beyond doubt.
You should pay attention to this word.
This word is like a lamp.
The lamp shines in a dark place.
You must pay attention until the day dawns.
You must pay attention until the morning star rises in your hearts.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔχομεν βεβαιότερον τὸν προφητικὸν λόγον ᾧ καλῶς ποιεῖτε προσέχοντες ὡς λύχνῳ φαίνοντι ἐν αὐχμηρῷ τόπῳ ἕως οὗ ἡμέρα διαυγάσῃ καὶ φωσφόρος ἀνατείλῃ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν

passages.text: Above all, you must understand that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one’s own interpretation.
passages.sermon:
Peter is speaking to Christians.
\r\nHe gives an important instruction.
\r\nYou must know this first.
\r\nNo prophecy in Scripture comes from a person’s own explanation.
\r\nEach prophecy does not come from private interpretation.
passages.original: τοῦτο πρῶτον γινώσκοντες ὅτι πᾶσα προφητεία γραφῆς ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως οὐ γίνεται

passages.text: For no such prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
No prophecy ever came by human will.
God did not let people invent prophecy themselves.
Men spoke words from God.
The Holy Spirit guided these men.
The Holy Spirit carried them as they spoke.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ θελήματι ἀνθρώπου ἠνέχθη προφητεία ποτέ ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου φερόμενοι ἐλάλησαν ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ἄνθρωποι
